messages:
customer-jane: Hi team — in our Private deployment the collector dies during debug bundle creation. It logs 'kms: access denied' and exits before upload. Request ID: 01KMS-ABCD1234. Can you advise? We're on v2.7.1 collector. Host: customer-pod-3.
maria (support): Thanks — can you paste collector stderr (journalctl) around the crash and the collector command you ran? Also confirm whether your deployment uses AWS KMS or GCP KMS.
customer-jane: aws kms. here's the log snippet:
```
[2026-03-16T12:02:11Z] collector ERROR: failed to encrypt manifest: AccessDeniedException: User: arn:aws:sts::123456789012:assumed-role/RedwoodCollectorRole is not authorized to perform: kms:Encrypt
request_id=01KMS-ABCD1234
stack=redwood/collector/encrypt.go:83
```
We run: /opt/redwood/collector/bin/collector --collect --output /tmp/debugbundle.tar.gz
kevin (sre): that error usually means the collector role can't use the key policy or CMK has a condition. Ask the customer to run a quick sts:GetCallerIdentity from the collector node to confirm role. Also check the CMK key policy for Principal.
customer-jane: ran from node:
```
$ aws sts get-caller-identity
{"Arn": "arn:aws:sts::123456789012:assumed-role/RedwoodCollectorRole/i-0abcd"}
```
Key is in same account, policy looks okay but there's a granting principal to account root — not sure.
jon (devex): to rule out encryption entirely, can you re-run collector with --skip-encrypt (temporary) and then attempt to upload via curl to our private upload endpoint so we test the network/path? Share curl -v output and any TLS errors.
customer-jane: tried:
```
$ /opt/redwood/collector/bin/collector --collect --skip-encrypt --output /tmp/debugbundle.tar.gz
Collector: bundle created /tmp/debugbundle.tar.gz
$ curl -v --cert /etc/redwood/client.pem --key /etc/redwood/client.key -F file=@/tmp/debugbundle.tar.gz "https://private-upload.redwood.example.com/upload?rid=01KMS-ABCD1234"
* TLSv1.3 (IN), TLS handshake, Newsession Ticket (0x0)
* TLSv1.3 (OUT), TLS handshake, Client hello (1)
* SSL: certificate verify failed (unknown CA)
* Closing connection 0
curl: (60) SSL certificate problem: unable to get local issuer certificate
```
So upload fails with cert verify.
maria (support): looks like mutual TLS is configured. Are you using the collector's runtime mTLS certs from the PKI setup? If customer-generated certs were rotated, the CA might not be trusted by our upload gateway.
kevin (sre): run this from the node to inspect the server cert chain:
```
$ openssl s_client -showcerts -connect private-upload.redwood.example.com:443 -servername private-upload.redwood.example.com
```
Also check /etc/ssl/certs/ for the CA that signed the client cert.
customer-jane: openssl output attached — server presents a cert signed by internal CA 'CorpRootCA' which we don't have mirrored on the collector. We use internal PKI so collector doesn't trust it by default.
jon (devex): two paths: (A) mirror the CorpRootCA into collector's trust store (trusted by curl/openssl) and re-run; or (B) we can provide a one-time presigned HTTPS URL that skips mTLS for support uploads. For immediate repro, option B is faster.
maria (support): I can spin a temporary upload token. But first, to help root cause the collector kms failure we still need to reproduce the encrypted path. Please run collector with REDWOOD_DEBUG=1 and attach the small debug log (<=1MB) to our support SFTP; I'll create a one-time SFTP user. For upload repro we can accept the unencrypted bundle via temporary HTTP token.
sre-bot: Incident #SUP-2026-142 created (severity: low). Assigned: maria, kevin. ETA for token: 15m.
maria (support): temporary HTTP token created: https://uploads.redwood.support/tmp/01KMS-ABCD1234?token=eyJtmp... Expires in 20m. Use curl without --cert: 
```
curl -v -F file=@/tmp/debugbundle.tar.gz "https://uploads.redwood.support/tmp/01KMS-ABCD1234?token=eyJtmp..."
```
I'll post result when bundle arrives.
customer-jane: uploading now — curl succeeds, server returns 200 and we see request id backend: RWB-9987. Upload done.
maria (support): got bundle RWB-9987. Quick triage: the bundle manifest shows redaction skipped three symlinked files and a fifo socket. Example in redaction_report.json: `skipped_symlink: ../app/.ssh -> sensitive` — that shouldn't crash encryption though. Kevin, I can reproduce KMS Deny when the collector assumes a role that isn't in the key policy's allowed principals.
kevin (sre): agreed — CMK likely restricts by role ARN. The fix: add arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/RedwoodCollectorRole to KeyPolicy or create grant for that role. I'll send customer a policy diff.
customer-jane: thanks — after we add the role to key policy I'll test. For our internal compliance we want collector not to accept mirroring CorpRootCA; we'll instead rotate the collector role permissions. One more ask: can you add warn-level log when redaction finds symlink so we catch it earlier?
jon (devex): opened ticket in repo: #652 add symlink warning + link to docs. Small patch incoming.
sre-bot: SUP-2026-142 updated: bundle stored RWB-9987, owner: customer-jane, next action: CMK policy update.
maria (support): closing loop — followups: maria to validate policy change, jon to land symlink warning, customer to retest. Thanks all :thumbsup:
